title: Flappy Flight
summary: Tap to flap a bird through gaps in the pipes. Gravity pulls, you push, and every pipe you pass scores once.
learn: make gravity pull with an acceleration, and flap by setting a speed
send clones from one hidden pipe, each at a random height
predict what a script does before you run it, then fix it
give every clone its own memory with sprite data

chapters.title: Fall and flap
chapters.idea: Gravity is an acceleration; a flap sets the speed.

chapters.title: Pipes
chapters.idea: A clone starts where its sprite is.

chapters.title: Score
chapters.idea: Each clone keeps its own data.

chapters.title: Win or lose
chapters.idea: You decide when the game ends.

steps.text: When the game starts, set the Bird’s ay to −900 and make it stop at the stage edge. Before you run it: what will the bird do?
steps.why: ay is an acceleration: gravity. It does not set a speed; it keeps adding downward speed, every moment.

checklist.text: The Bird stops at the stage edge

hints: In Physics, “set sprite … vx to …” has a menu: choose ay. Put it under “when game starts” from Events.
Set the Bird’s ay to −900. Then add “sprite Bird at stage edge stop” from Motion.

predict.question: What will the bird do?
choices: Fall faster and faster, then stop at the bottom
predict.explain: Gravity adds a little more downward speed every moment, so the bird falls faster and faster until the stage edge stops it.

steps.text: Flap: when space is pressed, set the Bird’s vy to 300 and play its flap animation. Run it, click the stage and keep the bird in the air.
steps.why: Setting vy gives one quick push up. Gravity then pulls the bird back down, and that push and fall is the whole game.

checklist.text: A script runs when space is pressed
It plays the Bird’s flap animation

hints: From Events, drag “when space key pressed”. In Physics, use “set sprite … vy to …” for the Bird.
Under it, add “play sprite Bird animation once and wait” from Looks. The Bird has two costumes: wings down, then wings up.

steps.text: The lesson wrote a loop that sends a pipe every 1.5 seconds, but every gap is at the same height. Fix it: before each clone, set Pipe’s y to a random number from −40 to 90.
steps.why: A clone starts where its sprite is. Pipe waits off the right edge, so every copy starts at Pipe’s height, until you move Pipe first.

checklist.text: Pipe moves to a random height in the loop

hints: Run it: the gaps line up, so you could fly straight through. What decides where each clone starts?
At the top of the loop, add “set sprite Pipe y to” from Motion, and put “random integer from −40 to 90” (Control) in it.

steps.text: Crash: when a Pipe touches the Bird, finish the game as a loss. And when the Bird’s y drops below −115, it hit the ground: finish the game too.
steps.why: The script belongs to Pipe, so every pipe clone checks for the bird. “When Bird updates” runs many times a second, so the ground is noticed at once.

checklist.text: When a Pipe touches the Bird, the game ends
Each update, the Bird checks for the ground

hints: Select Pipe, then from Events drag “when Pipe overlaps …” and choose Bird. Inside, put “finish game lose” from Game.
Select Bird and drag “when Bird updates”. Inside: if Bird’s y < −115, finish game lose.

steps.text: The lesson wrote a score script for Pipe: once a pipe is left of the bird (x below −150), add 1 to the score. It also destroys pipes that leave the stage. Before you run it: what will the score do when you pass a pipe?
steps.why: Read the script before you run it. Every pipe clone runs “when Pipe updates” for itself, about 30 times a second.
hints: Watch the score in the corner while a pipe slides past the bird.
How many updates happen after a pipe’s x drops below −150, before it leaves the stage?

predict.question: What will the score do when you pass a pipe?
choices: Go up by 1 for each pipe
Go up again and again for every pipe
predict.explain: Each update after the pipe passes adds another point: about 30 a second. The pipe needs to remember that it already scored.

steps.text: Give each pipe a memory. Pipe has data named “passed”, set to False. Score only when the pipe is past the bird and not “passed”, then set its “passed” to True.
steps.why: Every clone gets its own copy of its sprite’s data, so each pipe remembers for itself whether it has scored.

checklist.text: After scoring, it sets “passed” to True

hints: Select Pipe, press More settings and open “Sprite data & behavior”: its starting data has passed: false. In Game, “sprite … data named …” reads it and “set sprite … data named … to …” changes it.

From Logic, put “… and …” in the if: the x check on one side, “not (sprite this sprite data named passed)” on the other. Inside, after “change score by 1”, set this sprite’s data named passed to True (Logic).

steps.why: Click the stage, then tap space: little taps, not a long press. Each pipe scores once now.

steps.text: A goal to aim for: when the game starts, wait until the score reaches 10, then finish the game as a win.
steps.why: Flappy games never end by themselves. Your rule decides when a player has won.

checklist.text: Then finish the game as a win

hints: The idea card “Win screen” waits until the score reaches a number, then finishes the game.
Insert it, then change its 5 to 10 and write your own winning message.

steps.text: Play until the game ends: ten pipes to win, one bump to lose.
steps.why: Click the stage, then tap space to flap.

finish.text: A bird that falls and flaps, a stream of pipes at random heights, and a score that counts each pipe once.
remix: Tilt the bird: each update, set its direction from its vy, so it noses down as it falls.
Harder and harder: every 5 points, make the pipes a little faster or the gap a little smaller.
Coins in the gaps: clone a coin with each pipe and give an extra point for catching it.
